reason: Refuted AS WRITTEN. The idea itself is fine: a text-only post-deadline agenda with no build before 29 Sep, allowed by R8. The problem is that the action pre-registers G0 and the per-item gates NOW, and three of them are flawed. Pre-registering a flawed gate is the only real harm here. The EV-per-unit arithmetic checks out (2.0e-4, 0.9e-4, 0.89e-4, 0.72e-4, 0.6e-4, 0.17e-4). (1) G0 does not hold for the top-EV item. The D program's cost of about 20 GPU-h assumes '4 paired fine-tunes x ~1 h'. That is the exp23 recipe (1,200 iterations from the pilkwang weights), and those weights saw BOTH embryos, so 'train on A, score on B' is not held out. The finding itself says no leak-free baseline exists. The leak-free alternative is training from scratch on one embryo: 1.3 GPU-h per epoch (CONTEXT l.244), about 23 h per run (I-118). A 6bba-only scratch model after 5 epochs scored only 0.671 raw / 0.689 pp on LOEO 44b6 (A17, CONTEXT l.90). That makes 100+ GPU-h for 4 runs, not 20, with no local GPU and 30 GPU-h per week per account, and it measures a regime far from the 0.95 stack. Two precedents show that an honest weak-model arm-vs-control win in that regime did not transfer to the public stack: B5 AdaBN, +0.0073 on the 6bba-only scratch model, lost 0.0066 on the public stack (CONTEXT l.196), and B30 axis-flip, +0.0187 on an unseen-embryo scratch primary, was an LB tie (l.205). So G0 is either leaky at the stated cost, or unaffordable and has known false positives. (2) I-242 contradicts r12p-1. The fixed-node non-swap link oracle (+0.0011 bed-wide) is what r12p-1 uses to kill I-122 and I-285 as score levers, and a post-freeze re-solve on fixed nodes is under the same bound. Of the +0.0063 ceiling, 152 FP edges (0.0036) is edge dropping, the class that transferred at 0 (edge filter). With the item's own rule that more than 50% of the gain must come from TP edges, the most that can pass is about +0.002 at oracle. The realistic range +0.0005..+0.002 is therefore at the oracle limit, and #5 belongs at or below coordhead-v2. (3) The late-sub gates on #3, #5 and #8 (private delta >= +0.001) contradict r12p-4's own rule that items with a lab EV below +0.003 cannot be read and stay lab-only. At r = 1/6, their lab ranges (at most +0.003, +0.002 and +0.004) come to about +0.0003..+0.0007 public. Smaller issues. The I-222 gain arithmetic scales a between-clip FN gap that is confounded by clip difficulty (the r9 skeptic found 'no signal'). The 44b6 part of that gate reads the public (dorado) embryo, not the private ones. In R12P-2, P34->P35 and P38->P37 are the same mechanism on nearly the same base, so r_priv rests on about 2 independent pairs.
fix: Before pre-registering, amend the agenda text: (a) Split G0 into G0-FT and G0-SCR and label them honestly. G0-FT is a paired fine-tune from the public weights; call it 'leaky paired', fit only to KILL an item (arm <= control), never to pass one. G0-SCR is paired from-scratch on one embryo; cost it at >= 25 GPU-h per run, and require a transfer check on the full x138 stack (exp60, node count within +-1%) before any late sub, citing the B5 and B30 false positives. Re-cost the D program at 20 GPU-h (kill only) or ~100 GPU-h (pass), and put it after R12P-2 sets r. (b) Cap I-242 at the link-oracle bound (TP side <= +0.0011 bed-wide, passing max ~+0.002 at oracle), set EV to ~+0.0001, and rank it below coordhead-v2. (c) Remove the 'one late sub' step from #3, #5 and #8, or state it as a low-power sign check only (a displayed +0.001 proves a positive sign, while a 0 proves nothing), in line with r12p-4. (d) State that I-222's 44b6 arm reads the public embryo. Record kill criteria as written; they are sound.
realistic_gain: 0 on the public and private LB by construction (post-deadline, text only; finals #37 + #38 unchanged). Value is learning only. The amended G0 avoids spending about 20-100 GPU-h on a gate that is either leaky or has known false positives.
